source_review.notes: Checked the original Fowler/Hieatt/Mee Repository catalog entry, Evans' DDD Reference, related Fowler Data Mapper/Unit of Work/Identity Map material, Specification paper and current Microsoft DDD persistence guidance. ORM/provider behaviors remain explicitly version/configuration qualified.

evidence: Checked collection-like operation signatures and conditional version transition notation.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The collection metaphor is consistently qualified as observational rather than complexity/failure equivalence.

numerical_recomputation.notes: The chapter contains no quantitative claim whose validity depends on numerical calculation; the executable trace demonstrates categorical filtering/order/version behavior.

evidence: Verified conditional version update permits one conflicting writer to advance from a shared expected version under adequate local isolation.
Verified separate authorization pre-check plus unconstrained lookup admits disclosure/TOCTOU while a scoped predicate closes that path.
Verified per-method auto-commit counterexample breaks application-owned multi-operation/outbox atomicity.
Verified Identity Map premise supports one logical instance per scoped identity within one unit.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Query efficiency, isolation and substitution require implementation evidence beyond interface form.

evidence: Reviewed absent/forbidden concealment, tenant scope, authority change, version conflict, uniqueness/collation, empty/max page, deterministic ties and stale reads.
Reviewed lazy loading/N+1, unbounded queries, identity-map/no-tracking behavior, transaction rollback/outbox, cache scope, migration/restore and vendor error translation.
Reviewed fake/production divergence and regulated record break-glass/privacy cases.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Actual query plans, mapping, isolation, ORM tracking and database errors require real-adapter tests.

evidence: Traced inward interface ownership, aggregate-root mutation, scoped authorization, stable identity, concurrency control, query semantics, error translation and test parity throughout exposition/examples/answers.
Confirmed external APIs and read projections are not mislabeled aggregate repositories.
invariant_checking.notes: Repository cannot guarantee interchangeability across stores with different consistency/query capabilities.

evidence: Reviewed dependency-direction, aggregate, authorization, concurrency, identity, bounded-query and fake-substitution arguments against stated premises.
Confirmed counterexamples for repository-per-table, generic CRUD, arbitrary predicates, authorization pre-check, last-write-wins, lazy loading and weak in-memory fakes.
proof_review.notes: No formal proof of database serializability, query cost, legal authorization adequacy or universal adapter substitutability is claimed.

evidence: Audited collection-like, atomic, authorized, isolated, consistent, interchangeable, bounded, substitute and safe language.
Confirmed conceptual interface properties, implementation evidence and named review are separated.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: The chapter rejects Repository as mandatory ceremony or universal storage abstraction.

evidence: Reproduced tenant-a/t-b filtering, deterministic ID ordering and expected-1/actual-2 version conflict using Python 3.
Confirmed no database, transaction, concurrency, authorization, paging, mapper, identity map, failure or latency was executed.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Execution establishes fixed dictionary/filter/branch behavior only.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter preserves Repository's original domain collection/mapping intent while making aggregate, transaction, query, authorization, concurrency and cost boundaries explicit.

practitioner_review.notes: Guidance covers ownership, aggregate methods, query contracts, authorization predicates, Unit of Work/Identity Map, concurrency/error translation, CQRS, testing, performance and removal criteria.

pedagogical_review.notes: Objectives align with deterministic repository model, ten distinct cases and five exercises progressing from contract design through concurrency, diagnosis, boundary classification and regulated transfer.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
